import colorsys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.asarray(im).astype(np.float64)
H, W, _ = a.shape
print('image dims (W x H):', W, H)

col = a.mean(axis=0)  # (W, 3) average color of each column
diff = np.abs(np.diff(col, axis=0)).sum(axis=1)

# overall stats
overall = a.mean(axis=(0, 1))
h, s, v = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(*(overall / 255))
print(f'overall avg rgb=({overall[0]:.0f},{overall[1]:.0f},{overall[2]:.0f}) hue={h*360:.1f} sat={s:.3f} val={v:.3f}')

# saturation across all pixels
px = a.reshape(-1, 3) / 255.0
mx = px.max(axis=1); mn = px.min(axis=1)
sat = np.where(mx > 0, (mx - mn) / np.maximum(mx, 1e-9), 0)
print('pixel saturation: mean %.3f  p95 %.3f  max %.3f' % (sat.mean(), np.percentile(sat, 95), sat.max()))
lumsat = np.array([colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(*p) for p in px[::max(1, len(px)//20000)]])
print('pixel hue (deg) percentiles 5/50/95:', np.round(np.percentile(lumsat[:, 0] * 360, [5, 50, 95]), 1))

# stripe segmentation: cut where adjacent column colors change sharply
thr = max(diff.mean() + 2.0 * diff.std(), 8)
cand = np.where(diff > thr)[0]
groups = []
for b in cand:
    if groups and b - groups[-1][-1] <= 3:
        groups[-1].append(b)
    else:
        groups.append([b])
cuts = [int(np.mean(g)) for g in groups]
edges = [0] + cuts + [W]
print('num stripes:', len(edges) - 1)
if len(edges) - 1 < 200:
    for i, (s0, e0) in enumerate(zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:])):
        c = col[s0:e0].mean(axis=0)
        hh, ss, vv = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(*(c / 255))
        print(f'{i:3d} x={s0:4d}-{e0:4d} w={e0-s0:3d} rgb=({c[0]:5.1f},{c[1]:5.1f},{c[2]:5.1f}) hue={hh*360:5.1f} sat={ss:4.2f} val={vv:4.2f}')

"**Diamonds**" is a song recorded by the Barbadian singer [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna") as the lead single for her seventh album, *[Unapologetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unapologetic "Unapologetic")* (2012). [Sia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sia "Sia") wrote the track with the song's producers, [Benny Blanco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Blanco "Benny Blanco") and [Stargate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate_\(record_producers\) "Stargate (record producers)"). The song premiered on September 26, 2012, during the *[Elvis Duran and the Morning Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Duran_and_the_Morning_Show "Elvis Duran and the Morning Show")* and was digitally released the following day as the lead single from *Unapologetic*. "Diamonds" is a mid-tempo [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"), [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") and [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") [ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad") that features heavy [synthesizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer "Synthesizer"), orchestral sounds and electronic rhythms. The song's lyrics serve as a departure from the themes of unhealthy relationships that were on Rihanna's previous singles contrasted to the song's portrayal of lovers as "diamonds in the sky". [Music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_journalism "Music journalism") complimented the song's emotional depth and maturity, while also praising the lyrics and Rihanna's vocal performance, though others felt that it lacked the depth and punch when compared to her previous hits.

"Diamonds" topped music charts in over 20 countries, including the United States, where it became Rihanna's twelfth number 1 single on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and [tied her](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_number-one_singles "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") with [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna "Madonna") and [the Supremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Supremes "The Supremes") for the fifth-most number 1 singles in the chart's history. "Diamonds" was certified [Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) and sold over 3\.5 million digital copies in the country. It was also certified Diamond in Poland. It also peaked at number 1 on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") and became Rihanna's seventh number 1 song in the country; it was certified quadruple-times Platinum by the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") (BPI). By May 2013, it had sold over 7\.5 million copies worldwide.

The song's music video was shot by director [Anthony Mandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Mandler "Anthony Mandler"), a frequent collaborator of Rihanna's, and depicts her in four environments that represent the elements of earth, air, water, and fire. The video received positive reviews and was praised for its imagery. Some critics believe that the heavily tattooed man intertwined with Rihanna's arm in the video resembles [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown"). The singer performed "Diamonds" on television shows such as *[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")* and *[The X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_X_Factor_\(British_TV_series\) "The X Factor (British TV series)")* and included it on the [777](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/777_Tour "777 Tour"), [Diamonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamonds_World_Tour "Diamonds World Tour"), [Monster Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Monster_Tour_\(Eminem_and_Rihanna\) "The Monster Tour (Eminem and Rihanna)") and the [Anti World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti_World_Tour "Anti World Tour") [set lists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_list "Set list"). The [American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_of_Composers,_Authors_and_Publishers "American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers") (ASCAP) recognized it as one of the most performed songs of 2013 and 2014\. The official remix of "Diamonds" featured rapper [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West") and was released on November 16, 2012\. The song has been covered by various recording artists, including [Josef Salvat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josef_Salvat "Josef Salvat"), who released his own cover of "Diamonds" as a single.It has currently surpassed 2 billion streams on Spotify.

## Writing and production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Writing and production")\]

[![A blonde woman wearing a white dress is performing](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Sia_Furler_in_concert.jpg/250px-Sia_Furler_in_concert.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sia_Furler_in_concert.jpg)

[Sia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sia "Sia") (*pictured*) wrote the lyrics, while producer [Benny Blanco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Blanco "Benny Blanco") co-wrote and co-produced "Diamonds" with [Stargate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate_\(record_producers\) "Stargate (record producers)").

In 2012, American songwriter and record producer [Benny Blanco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Blanco "Benny Blanco") met with Norwegian production duo [Stargate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate_\(record_producers\) "Stargate (record producers)") at a recording studio in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") to write new songs, including one for Rihanna.[\[1\]](#cite_note-the_source-1) Stargate had previously produced her singles "[Don't Stop the Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Stop_the_Music_\(Rihanna_song\) "Don't Stop the Music (Rihanna song)")" (2007) and "[Only Girl (In the World)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Girl_\(In_the_World\) "Only Girl (In the World)")" (2010).[\[2\]](#cite_note-daily_news-2) According to Blanco, he and Stargate wanted to deviate from Rihanna's usual sound and produce as though the song would be for a rapper such as [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West"): "It's the one that we weren't thinking Rihanna ... that turned into the Rihanna record ... But that's how it always happens... with me".[\[1\]](#cite_note-the_source-1) They produced the song's drum machine beat after the other instrumental music was recorded.[\[1\]](#cite_note-the_source-1)

Stargate's Mikkel Eriksen told *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* that Blanco took a recorded snippet of Eriksen's singing, altered it electronically, and made it sound "dirtier".[\[3\]](#cite_note-ny_times_benny-3) He then applied timbre and used audio software to create ghostly accompaniment lines. Eriksen described Blanco's style as "unorthodox, as he almost never plays the keyboards but throws in weird samples and alters them to the right pitch to go with the song."[\[3\]](#cite_note-ny_times_benny-3) Australian singer-songwriter [Sia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sia "Sia") later joined them and wrote the lyrics for "Diamonds" in 14 minutes.[\[1\]](#cite_note-the_source-1)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

After the song was completed, they wanted to play it to Rihanna, but Blanco was skeptical about the reaction towards the song because of its slow sound. After Stargate played it to her, they called Blanco from [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") and told him that she liked the song: "She's flippin' out. She played it like seven times in a row. It's her favorite song."[\[1\]](#cite_note-the_source-1) Phil Tan and the assistant Daniela Rivera, mixed and mastered "Diamonds".[\[5\]](#cite_note-Notes-5) Rihanna attempted to emulate Sia's singing style, which reportedly led to Sia thinking that her own vocal recording had been released.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) Recalling it, in an interview with *[The Huffington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Huffington_Post "The Huffington Post")*, Blanco commented, "We needed to have it recorded, the beat finished, mixed and mastered in 24 hours. She was recording in a separate part of the world, sending back the files, we're finishing the music and then we're mixing and mastering it, and then it was out in a few days. It's fucking amazing and incredible."[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) [Kuk Harrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuk_Harrell "Kuk Harrell") produced Rihanna's vocals on the song and recorded them together with Marcos Tovar.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Notes-5)

In 2021, Blanco said that Rihanna was not who he had in mind for the track initially. He considered [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West") or [Lana Del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lana_Del_Rey "Lana Del Rey") but Stargate was adamant it should be Rihanna. He also revealed that [Eminem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eminem "Eminem") recorded a song on the beat.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

The lyrics are very hopeful and positive, but it's about love."[\[11\]](#cite_note-happy-11)

The single's cover artwork was revealed on September 24 and depicted Rihanna rolling diamonds in a manner suggestive of [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_\(cannabis\) "Joint (cannabis)") rolling.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) On September 26, Rihanna posted the full lyrics of the song in a [PDF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDF_format "PDF format") on her official website Rihanna7.com.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) "Diamonds" premiered the same day on the *[Elvis Duran and the Morning Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Duran_and_the_Morning_Show "Elvis Duran and the Morning Show")*,[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) and on the following day, it was released as a [digital download](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download "Music download") on the [7 Digital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_Digital "7 Digital") store.[\[16\]](#cite_note-7_digital-16) In the United Kingdom, the song was released to 7 Digital on September 28\.[\[17\]](#cite_note-uk_release-17) [Def Jam Recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Def_Jam_Recordings "Def Jam Recordings") solicited the single to [mainstream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") and [rhythmic contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary "Rhythmic contemporary") radio formats in the United States on October 2\.[\[18\]](#cite_note-FMQB-18) On November 5, it was released in Germany as a [CD single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD_single "CD single"), which also contained the song's Bimbo Jones vocal remix.[\[19\]](#cite_note-cd_single-19) On December 18, eight digital remixes of the single were digitally released.[\[20\]](#cite_note-remixes-20)

"Diamonds" has a length of three minutes and forty-five seconds.[\[16\]](#cite_note-7_digital-16) The lyrics are composed in two main stanzas with the repetition of the chorus sung six times in the song using variations of the main verse depicting "diamonds in the sky".[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) [Allmusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allmusic "Allmusic") critic Andy Kellman characterized it as a mid-tempo pop ballad,[\[22\]](#cite_note-allmusic_review-22) while Michael Baggs of [Gigwise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigwise "Gigwise") described it as a mid-tempo [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") song.[\[23\]](#cite_note-gigwise-23) *[Time Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Out_\(magazine\) "Time Out (magazine)")*'s James Manning described the song as a "somber" [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") ballad.[\[24\]](#cite_note-time_out-24) It features heavy [synthesizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer "Synthesizer"),[\[25\]](#cite_note-billboard-25) orchestral sounds and electronic rhythms accompanying Rihanna's vocal performance.[\[26\]](#cite_note-stone-26) *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* magazine wrote that "the track's production mainly stays out of Rihanna's way, letting the pop star build hooks with layers of her voice."[\[26\]](#cite_note-stone-26) In a review of *Unapologetic*, Stacy-Ann Ellis of *[Vibe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibe_\(magazine\) "Vibe (magazine)")* noted that an improvement in the singer's singing is evidenced by ballads such as "Diamonds" and "[Stay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stay_\(Rihanna_song\) "Stay (Rihanna song)")". According to [EMI Music Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMI_Music "EMI Music")'s digital sheet music for the song, "Diamonds" is composed in the [key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_\(music\) "Key (music)") of [B minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B_minor "B minor") and set in [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_time "Common time") signature, and has a moderately slow [groove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groove_\(music\) "Groove (music)") of 92 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo").[\[27\]](#cite_note-musicnotes-27) Rihanna's vocals span from the low note of [F♯3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F♯_\(musical_note\) "F♯ (musical note)") to the high note of [F♯5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F♯_\(musical_note\) "F♯ (musical note)").[\[27\]](#cite_note-musicnotes-27)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

In a positive review of the song, Robert Copsey of *[Digital Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Spy "Digital Spy")* gave it four out of five stars and praised Rihanna's direction towards a "softer and more prolific edge".[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) Brittany Lewis of GlobalGrind called "Diamonds" a catchy song and felt that it had the potential to be another hit for Rihanna.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) Glenn Gamboa of *[Newsday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsday "Newsday")* said that, although it does not sound like an emphatic hit, the lyrical content of the song depicts a "personal shift" for Rihanna.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) According to James Montgomery of MTV News, "Diamonds" is more positive than previous singles such as "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")" and "[Where Have You Been](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_Have_You_Been "Where Have You Been")", despite its moderate tempo.[\[31\]](#cite_note-mtv1-31) Lindsey DiMattina of Hollywood.com said that Rihanna's singing is stronger than ever.[\[32\]](#cite_note-hollywoord-32) [Contactmusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contactmusic.com "Contactmusic.com")'s reviewer described it as a "laid-back track", and suggested that the lyrical content is related to her former boyfriend [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown_\(American_entertainer\) "Chris Brown (American entertainer)").[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) In a track-by-track review of *Unapologetic*, Andrew Hampp of *Billboard* found the song inspiring and commented that it "finds Rihanna doing one of her throatiest, most impassioned vocals to date".[\[34\]](#cite_note-billboardtrackbytrackreview-34) Andy Kellman of Allmusic cited the song as one of the highlights on *Unapologetic*,[\[22\]](#cite_note-allmusic_review-22) and gave it three and a half stars.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35)

In a less enthusiastic critique, [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") of *The New York Times* likened "Diamonds" to a [*James Bond* movie theme song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Bond_music "James Bond music"), but with "insipid lyrics".[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) Jim Farber of the *[New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_News_\(New_York\) "Daily News (New York)")* felt that the song is not as evocative as it attempts to be and lacks the sense of mystery and engaging production found on "We Found Love".[\[2\]](#cite_note-daily_news-2) Kevin Blair of the *[Irish Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Independent "Irish Independent")*'s, Independent Woman, was critical of the song and dismissed it as a "chugging, faintly misty-eyed, middle of the road pop song".[\[37\]](#cite_note-independent.ie-37) Chris Richards of *[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")* panned the song as a "power ballad without much power".[\[38\]](#cite_note-38)

### North America

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: North America")\]

[![A blond woman wearing a jeweled black stage outfit plays a black guitar and sings into a microphone.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/MadonnaO2171023_%285_of_133%29_%2853270847219%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-MadonnaO2171023_%285_of_133%29_%2853270847219%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MadonnaO2171023_\(5_of_133\)_\(53270847219\)_\(cropped\).jpg)

"Diamonds" became Rihanna's twelfth number 1 on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), tying her with [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna "Madonna") (*pictured*) and [the Supremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Supremes "The Supremes") as the artists with the fifth-most number 1 singles in the chart's history.

In the US, "Diamonds" debuted at number 16 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and sold 133,000 copies in its first week.[\[51\]](#cite_note-51) In its fourth week, it climbed to number 8 on the chart and became Rihanna's twenty-third top-ten single.[\[52\]](#cite_note-TopTen-52) For the week ending December 1, 2012, the song became Rihanna's twelfth number 1 on the chart, which ended the nine-week reign of [Maroon 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maroon_5 "Maroon 5")'s "[One More Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_More_Night_\(Maroon_5_song\) "One More Night (Maroon 5 song)")".[\[53\]](#cite_note-us_sales-53) With the feat, Rihanna tied [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna "Madonna") and [the Supremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Supremes "The Supremes") as the [artists with the fifth-most number 1 singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_number-one_singles "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") in the chart's history. Rihanna also passed [Mariah Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey") as the female artist to mark twelve number 1 songs the fastest on the chart by achieving the feat in six years and seven months, which bested Carey's stretch of more than seven years.[\[54\]](#cite_note-number_1-54) "Diamonds" charted for three consecutive weeks atop the Hot 100, while her album *Unapologetic* topped the [*Billboard* 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"). As a result, Rihanna became only the second artist of 2012 to top both the *Billboard* singles and albums charts simultaneously; the first to do so was English singer [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele").[\[55\]](#cite_note-BillboardDouble-55)

On the [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart, "Diamonds" debuted at number 28\. In its fourth week, it climbed to number 10, becoming Rihanna's 19th top ten, breaking a tie with [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne") for the second-best sum in the list's 22-year history; only Mariah Carey (23) has more.[\[56\]](#cite_note-56) For the issue dated December 15, the song topped the chart, becoming Rihanna's tenth number 1 and placing second for female artists with the most chart toppers, only behind Mariah Carey (11).[\[57\]](#cite_note-Trust-57) On the [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40") chart, "Diamonds" debuted at number 29, extending Rihanna's lead as the artist with the most appearances on the chart.[\[58\]](#cite_note-PopDebut-58) On October 11, 2012, *Billboard* unveiled new methodology for the [Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") chart, newly factoring digital download sales and streaming data into the 50-position rankings, along with existing radio airplay data monitored by [Nielsen BDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_BDS "Nielsen BDS"). Due to this, "Diamonds" saw a huge leap from number 66 to number 1,[\[59\]](#cite_note-R&BNumberOne-59) marking Rihanna's second single as a lead artist to top the chart;[\[60\]](#cite_note-US_Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs-60) it topped the chart for fourteen consecutive weeks.[\[61\]](#cite_note-61) "Diamonds" topped the [Dance Club Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs") chart, becoming Rihanna's nineteenth number 1, tying her with [Janet Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Jackson "Janet Jackson") for the second-most number 1 songs in the chart's 36-year history. Only Madonna has more (49).[\[62\]](#cite_note-DanceNumberOne-62) "Diamonds" is, since 2024, [certified diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_certification "Music certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA).[\[63\]](#cite_note-RIAA-63)

In Canada, the song debuted at number 9 on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100") for the issue dated October 13, 2012\.[\[64\]](#cite_note-64) The song peaked at number 1 on the issue dated November 24, 2012, becoming Rihanna's sixth single to reach number 1 on the chart.[\[65\]](#cite_note-Canada-65) It remained atop of it for four consecutive weeks.[\[66\]](#cite_note-66) It was certified Gold by [Music Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Canada "Music Canada") denoting sales of over 40,000 copies.[\[67\]](#cite_note-Music_Canada-67)

### Europe and Oceania

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Europe and Oceania")\]

"Diamonds" made its first chart appearance in Ireland on September 27, 2012, where it debuted at number 17\.[\[68\]](#cite_note-Ireland_debut-68) It reached its peak of number 2 on October 25, 2012\.[\[69\]](#cite_note-69) The single debuted at number 1 on both the United Kingdom's pop and R&B singles charts on October 7, 2012, with over 105,000 copies sold. This gave Rihanna her seventh number 1 single in the country.[\[70\]](#cite_note-70)[\[71\]](#cite_note-71) After nine weeks on the pop chart, "Diamonds" rose from number 10 to 3, following Rihanna's performance of the song on *[The X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_X_Factor_\(British_TV_series\) "The X Factor (British TV series)")* the previous week.[\[72\]](#cite_note-72) From its debut, the song remained atop the R&B chart for three consecutive weeks before being deposed of the top spot by [Labrinth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrinth "Labrinth") and [Emeli Sandé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emeli_Sandé "Emeli Sandé")'s "[Beneath Your Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beneath_Your_Beautiful "Beneath Your Beautiful")".[\[73\]](#cite_note-73) As of March 2014[\[update\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit), "Diamonds" has sold over one million copies in the UK, and became Rihanna's fourth single to achieve that feat. With that, she became only the second artist to have four million-selling singles in the UK, only behind [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles"), who have six.[\[74\]](#cite_note-uk_million-74)

"Diamonds" debuted at number 1 in France, becoming Rihanna's fourth number 1 single in the country and remaining at the top spot for three consecutive weeks.[\[75\]](#cite_note-France-75) "Diamonds" also peaked at number 1 in Germany for ten consecutive weeks, becoming Rihanna's fifth number 1 single in the country and surpassing "Umbrella" (2007) as her longest-running German number 1 single.[\[76\]](#cite_note-German_Discography-76) The song was placed at number 7 on the German 2012 Year-End singles chart and was certified Platinum, denoting sales of 300,000 copies in the country.[\[77\]](#cite_note-GermanyPlatinum-77) "Diamonds" remained number 1 in Norway for eleven consecutive weeks,[\[78\]](#cite_note-Norway-78) the Czech Republic for eight,[\[79\]](#cite_note-CzechRepublic-79) Denmark for six,[\[80\]](#cite_note-Denmark-80) Switzerland for five,[\[81\]](#cite_note-Switzerland-81) Austria for four,[\[82\]](#cite_note-Austria-82) Finland for three weeks[\[83\]](#cite_note-Finland-83) and Scotland one.[\[84\]](#cite_note-84)

"Diamonds" entered the [New Zealand Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Singles_Chart "New Zealand Singles Chart") at number 5 on October 8, 2012\. After eight weeks in the top ten, the song peaked at number 2\.[\[85\]](#cite_note-NZ-85) The single has received a double-Platinum certification from the [Recording Industry Association of New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_New_Zealand "Recording Industry Association of New Zealand"), denoting sales of 30,000 copies.[\[86\]](#cite_note-new_zealand_cert-86) "Diamonds" debuted at number 8 on the [Australian Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") on October 14, 2012\. The song reached a peak of number 6 on November 4, 2012\.[\[87\]](#cite_note-Australia-87) The song has been certified 13× Platinum by the [Australian Recording Industry Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Recording_Industry_Association "Australian Recording Industry Association") (ARIA), denoting 910,000 equivalent units.[\[88\]](#cite_note-cert-88) By May 2013, it had sold over 7\.5 million copies worldwide.[\[89\]](#cite_note-89)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Music video")\]

### Background and concept

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Background and concept")\]

> "With every song it's a different story, so the visuals are very specific to that story and that world. With 'Diamonds,' it was just a series of vignettes that we put together to help get the emotion across throughout the song 'cause the song changes and it builds, and there's no real way that you could do that."

— Rihanna explaining the concept for the music video.[\[90\]](#cite_note-MTVVena-90)

Rihanna began to film the [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "Diamonds" on October 21, 2012, at the [Mojave Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojave_Desert "Mojave Desert") in [Lancaster, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancaster,_California "Lancaster, California").[\[31\]](#cite_note-mtv1-31) It was directed by her regular collaborator [Anthony Mandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Mandler "Anthony Mandler"), who previously directed her videos for "[Russian Roulette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Roulette_\(Rihanna_song\) "Russian Roulette (Rihanna song)")" (2009) and "[Man Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_Down_\(song\) "Man Down (song)")" (2011).[\[31\]](#cite_note-mtv1-31) Photographs of the production leaked to the press the same day and showed Rihanna in a white and black dress in front of a fire. Ethan Sacks of the *New York Daily News* remarked that she "looked like a gem on the set of her video shoot."[\[91\]](#cite_note-91) Rihanna said that she wanted the video's abstract scenes to capture the appropriate emotion for the audience.[\[90\]](#cite_note-MTVVena-90) Mandler sought to create a "wider landscape" by suggesting and transfiguring ideas for viewers through the video: "\[T\]hey needed to feel like dream vignettes, like, when you wake up from a dream, you realize what you were dreaming about is not really what it was about, it was about something else."[\[92\]](#cite_note-Mandler-92) He also tried to relate the video's concept to Rihanna's personal life: "What's truth or fiction? You know 'Is she drowning, or is she in complete ecstasy? Are those hands coming apart, or are they finding each other?' ... we tried to bring up these deeper questions that relate to the song and her life and finding beauty in chaos and finding beauty in pain and finding pain in beauty."[\[92\]](#cite_note-Mandler-92) On November 7, a behind-the-scenes video was posted on [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")'s official website.[\[93\]](#cite_note-premiere-93) It featured Rihanna in a "leopard-print" robe as she emerged from a trailer and headed to the shooting set. The scenes were intercut with police officers who chase armed fighters. Rihanna stands in a deserted landscape in the video's other scenes.[\[93\]](#cite_note-premiere-93) The music video for "Diamonds" premiered November 8 on MTV. The video was also made available for [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") at Rihanna.MTV.com.[\[93\]](#cite_note-premiere-93) It was digitally released on November 14 via the [iTunes Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes_Store "ITunes Store").[\[94\]](#cite_note-94)

### Synopsis

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Synopsis")\]

[![A screenshot of two tattooed hands intertwining](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e1/Diamonds_video_shoot.png/330px-Diamonds_video_shoot.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Diamonds_video_shoot.png)

A screenshot from the music video showing Rihanna's hand intertwined with that of a heavily tattooed man. Some critics believed the arm of the man resembled that of [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown").[\[95\]](#cite_note-nbc_review-95)

The music video opens with a view of Rihanna lying in open waters, as other scenes of diamonds being rolled in a manner suggestive of making a joint are intercut – a scene reminiscent of the single's artwork. As the video progresses Rihanna is shown running on a highway. In a [black-and-white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black-and-white "Black-and-white") scene, Rihanna licks the joint and begins smoking it. The image fades to black as the song begins. Rihanna performs in the same black-and-white setting while in a black corset. Images of Rihanna on a bed in a room while singing are shown, with objects breaking, curtains falling and roses burning in [reverse effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backwards_masking "Backwards masking"). Rihanna is shown again on the highway, running away from what appears to be the headlights of a chasing car. She then stops as she looks up to the night sky at an [aurora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_\(astronomy\) "Aurora (astronomy)") view. Throughout the video, Rihanna's hand is shown intertwined with that of a heavily tattooed man, whose face is not shown in the video. As the second verse starts, Rihanna is shown in a desert where horses run freely. Scenes of a street battle are later shown, depicting burning cars and broken glass around the environment. As the video continues, the singer and her lover's hands are shown slowly slipping apart, with only their fingertips touching towards the conclusion of the video. The video ends with Rihanna once again floating alone in the open waters.

"**Diamonds**" is a song recorded by the Barbadian singer [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna") as the lead single for her seventh album, *[Unapologetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unapologetic "Unapologetic")* (2012). [Sia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sia "Sia") wrote the track with the song's producers, [Benny Blanco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Blanco "Benny Blanco") and [Stargate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate_\(record_producers\) "Stargate (record producers)"). The song premiered on September 26, 2012, during the *[Elvis Duran and the Morning Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Duran_and_the_Morning_Show "Elvis Duran and the Morning Show")* and was digitally released the following day as the lead single from *Unapologetic*. "Diamonds" is a mid-tempo [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"), [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") and [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") [ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad") that features heavy [synthesizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer "Synthesizer"), orchestral sounds and electronic rhythms. The song's lyrics serve as a departure from the themes of unhealthy relationships that were on Rihanna's previous singles contrasted to the song's portrayal of lovers as "diamonds in the sky". [Music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_journalism "Music journalism") complimented the song's emotional depth and maturity, while also praising the lyrics and Rihanna's vocal performance, though others felt that it lacked the depth and punch when compared to her previous hits.

"Diamonds" topped music charts in over 20 countries, including the United States, where it became Rihanna's twelfth number 1 single on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and [tied her](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_number-one_singles "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") with [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna "Madonna") and [the Supremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Supremes "The Supremes") for the fifth-most number 1 singles in the chart's history. "Diamonds" was certified [Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) and sold over 3\.5 million digital copies in the country. It was also certified Diamond in Poland. It also peaked at number 1 on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") and became Rihanna's seventh number 1 song in the country; it was certified quadruple-times Platinum by the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") (BPI). By May 2013, it had sold over 7\.5 million copies worldwide.

The song's music video was shot by director [Anthony Mandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Mandler "Anthony Mandler"), a frequent collaborator of Rihanna's, and depicts her in four environments that represent the elements of earth, air, water, and fire. The video received positive reviews and was praised for its imagery. Some critics believe that the heavily tattooed man intertwined with Rihanna's arm in the video resembles [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown"). The singer performed "Diamonds" on television shows such as *[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")* and *[The X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_X_Factor_\(British_TV_series\) "The X Factor (British TV series)")* and included it on the [777](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/777_Tour "777 Tour"), [Diamonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamonds_World_Tour "Diamonds World Tour"), [Monster Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Monster_Tour_\(Eminem_and_Rihanna\) "The Monster Tour (Eminem and Rihanna)") and the [Anti World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti_World_Tour "Anti World Tour") [set lists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_list "Set list"). The [American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_of_Composers,_Authors_and_Publishers "American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers") (ASCAP) recognized it as one of the most performed songs of 2013 and 2014\. The official remix of "Diamonds" featured rapper [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West") and was released on November 16, 2012\. The song has been covered by various recording artists, including [Josef Salvat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josef_Salvat "Josef Salvat"), who released his own cover of "Diamonds" as a single.It has currently surpassed 2 billion streams on Spotify.

## Writing and production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Writing and production")\]

[![A blonde woman wearing a white dress is performing](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Sia_Furler_in_concert.jpg/250px-Sia_Furler_in_concert.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sia_Furler_in_concert.jpg)

[Sia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sia "Sia") (*pictured*) wrote the lyrics, while producer [Benny Blanco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Blanco "Benny Blanco") co-wrote and co-produced "Diamonds" with [Stargate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate_\(record_producers\) "Stargate (record producers)").

In 2012, American songwriter and record producer [Benny Blanco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Blanco "Benny Blanco") met with Norwegian production duo [Stargate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate_\(record_producers\) "Stargate (record producers)") at a recording studio in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") to write new songs, including one for Rihanna.[\[1\]](#cite_note-the_source-1) Stargate had previously produced her singles "[Don't Stop the Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Stop_the_Music_\(Rihanna_song\) "Don't Stop the Music (Rihanna song)")" (2007) and "[Only Girl (In the World)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Girl_\(In_the_World\) "Only Girl (In the World)")" (2010).[\[2\]](#cite_note-daily_news-2) According to Blanco, he and Stargate wanted to deviate from Rihanna's usual sound and produce as though the song would be for a rapper such as [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West"): "It's the one that we weren't thinking Rihanna ... that turned into the Rihanna record ... But that's how it always happens... with me".[\[1\]](#cite_note-the_source-1) They produced the song's drum machine beat after the other instrumental music was recorded.[\[1\]](#cite_note-the_source-1)

Stargate's Mikkel Eriksen told *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* that Blanco took a recorded snippet of Eriksen's singing, altered it electronically, and made it sound "dirtier".[\[3\]](#cite_note-ny_times_benny-3) He then applied timbre and used audio software to create ghostly accompaniment lines. Eriksen described Blanco's style as "unorthodox, as he almost never plays the keyboards but throws in weird samples and alters them to the right pitch to go with the song."[\[3\]](#cite_note-ny_times_benny-3) Australian singer-songwriter [Sia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sia "Sia") later joined them and wrote the lyrics for "Diamonds" in 14 minutes.[\[1\]](#cite_note-the_source-1)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

After the song was completed, they wanted to play it to Rihanna, but Blanco was skeptical about the reaction towards the song because of its slow sound. After Stargate played it to her, they called Blanco from [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") and told him that she liked the song: "She's flippin' out. She played it like seven times in a row. It's her favorite song."[\[1\]](#cite_note-the_source-1) Phil Tan and the assistant Daniela Rivera, mixed and mastered "Diamonds".[\[5\]](#cite_note-Notes-5) Rihanna attempted to emulate Sia's singing style, which reportedly led to Sia thinking that her own vocal recording had been released.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) Recalling it, in an interview with *[The Huffington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Huffington_Post "The Huffington Post")*, Blanco commented, "We needed to have it recorded, the beat finished, mixed and mastered in 24 hours. She was recording in a separate part of the world, sending back the files, we're finishing the music and then we're mixing and mastering it, and then it was out in a few days. It's fucking amazing and incredible."[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) [Kuk Harrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuk_Harrell "Kuk Harrell") produced Rihanna's vocals on the song and recorded them together with Marcos Tovar.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Notes-5)

In 2021, Blanco said that Rihanna was not who he had in mind for the track initially. He considered [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West") or [Lana Del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lana_Del_Rey "Lana Del Rey") but Stargate was adamant it should be Rihanna. He also revealed that [Eminem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eminem "Eminem") recorded a song on the beat.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

## Release and artwork

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Release and artwork")\]

> "I think a lot of people are afraid of being happy because of what others might think of it. ... They're afraid to embrace that and embrace themselves and love themselves and do what they love and do what makes them happy."

— Rihanna talking about the lyrical meaning behind "Diamonds" for [MTV News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_News "MTV News").[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

On September 12, 2012, Def Jam France announced via [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") that Rihanna would release a new single the following week and that her seventh studio album would be released in November. However, the tweet was shortly deleted and replaced with another clarifying that more information would be given on September 13\.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) In an interview with [iHeartRadio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio "IHeartRadio") at their annual music festival in September, Rihanna confirmed "Diamonds" as her new single and said that it would first be played on American radio, beginning on September 26\.[\[11\]](#cite_note-happy-11) She described it as an easy-going, but optimistic song that is "happy and hippy" rather than dance-oriented and said that the song "gives me such a great feeling when I listen to it. The lyrics are very hopeful and positive, but it's about love."[\[11\]](#cite_note-happy-11)

The single's cover artwork was revealed on September 24 and depicted Rihanna rolling diamonds in a manner suggestive of [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_\(cannabis\) "Joint (cannabis)") rolling.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) On September 26, Rihanna posted the full lyrics of the song in a [PDF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDF_format "PDF format") on her official website Rihanna7.com.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) "Diamonds" premiered the same day on the *[Elvis Duran and the Morning Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Duran_and_the_Morning_Show "Elvis Duran and the Morning Show")*,[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) and on the following day, it was released as a [digital download](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download "Music download") on the [7 Digital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_Digital "7 Digital") store.[\[16\]](#cite_note-7_digital-16) In the United Kingdom, the song was released to 7 Digital on September 28\.[\[17\]](#cite_note-uk_release-17) [Def Jam Recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Def_Jam_Recordings "Def Jam Recordings") solicited the single to [mainstream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") and [rhythmic contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary "Rhythmic contemporary") radio formats in the United States on October 2\.[\[18\]](#cite_note-FMQB-18) On November 5, it was released in Germany as a [CD single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD_single "CD single"), which also contained the song's Bimbo Jones vocal remix.[\[19\]](#cite_note-cd_single-19) On December 18, eight digital remixes of the single were digitally released.[\[20\]](#cite_note-remixes-20)

"Diamonds" has a length of three minutes and forty-five seconds.[\[16\]](#cite_note-7_digital-16) The lyrics are composed in two main stanzas with the repetition of the chorus sung six times in the song using variations of the main verse depicting "diamonds in the sky".[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) [Allmusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allmusic "Allmusic") critic Andy Kellman characterized it as a mid-tempo pop ballad,[\[22\]](#cite_note-allmusic_review-22) while Michael Baggs of [Gigwise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigwise "Gigwise") described it as a mid-tempo [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") song.[\[23\]](#cite_note-gigwise-23) *[Time Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Out_\(magazine\) "Time Out (magazine)")*'s James Manning described the song as a "somber" [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") ballad.[\[24\]](#cite_note-time_out-24) It features heavy [synthesizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer "Synthesizer"),[\[25\]](#cite_note-billboard-25) orchestral sounds and electronic rhythms accompanying Rihanna's vocal performance.[\[26\]](#cite_note-stone-26) *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* magazine wrote that "the track's production mainly stays out of Rihanna's way, letting the pop star build hooks with layers of her voice."[\[26\]](#cite_note-stone-26) In a review of *Unapologetic*, Stacy-Ann Ellis of *[Vibe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibe_\(magazine\) "Vibe (magazine)")* noted that an improvement in the singer's singing is evidenced by ballads such as "Diamonds" and "[Stay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stay_\(Rihanna_song\) "Stay (Rihanna song)")". According to [EMI Music Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMI_Music "EMI Music")'s digital sheet music for the song, "Diamonds" is composed in the [key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_\(music\) "Key (music)") of [B minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B_minor "B minor") and set in [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_time "Common time") signature, and has a moderately slow [groove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groove_\(music\) "Groove (music)") of 92 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo").[\[27\]](#cite_note-musicnotes-27) Rihanna's vocals span from the low note of [F♯3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F♯_\(musical_note\) "F♯ (musical note)") to the high note of [F♯5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F♯_\(musical_note\) "F♯ (musical note)").[\[27\]](#cite_note-musicnotes-27)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

In a positive review of the song, Robert Copsey of *[Digital Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Spy "Digital Spy")* gave it four out of five stars and praised Rihanna's direction towards a "softer and more prolific edge".[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) Brittany Lewis of GlobalGrind called "Diamonds" a catchy song and felt that it had the potential to be another hit for Rihanna.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) Glenn Gamboa of *[Newsday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsday "Newsday")* said that, although it does not sound like an emphatic hit, the lyrical content of the song depicts a "personal shift" for Rihanna.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) According to James Montgomery of MTV News, "Diamonds" is more positive than previous singles such as "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")" and "[Where Have You Been](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_Have_You_Been "Where Have You Been")", despite its moderate tempo.[\[31\]](#cite_note-mtv1-31) Lindsey DiMattina of Hollywood.com said that Rihanna's singing is stronger than ever.[\[32\]](#cite_note-hollywoord-32) [Contactmusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contactmusic.com "Contactmusic.com")'s reviewer described it as a "laid-back track", and suggested that the lyrical content is related to her former boyfriend [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown_\(American_entertainer\) "Chris Brown (American entertainer)").[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) In a track-by-track review of *Unapologetic*, Andrew Hampp of *Billboard* found the song inspiring and commented that it "finds Rihanna doing one of her throatiest, most impassioned vocals to date".[\[34\]](#cite_note-billboardtrackbytrackreview-34) Andy Kellman of Allmusic cited the song as one of the highlights on *Unapologetic*,[\[22\]](#cite_note-allmusic_review-22) and gave it three and a half stars.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35)

In a less enthusiastic critique, [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") of *The New York Times* likened "Diamonds" to a [*James Bond* movie theme song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Bond_music "James Bond music"), but with "insipid lyrics".[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) Jim Farber of the *[New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_News_\(New_York\) "Daily News (New York)")* felt that the song is not as evocative as it attempts to be and lacks the sense of mystery and engaging production found on "We Found Love".[\[2\]](#cite_note-daily_news-2) Kevin Blair of the *[Irish Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Independent "Irish Independent")*'s, Independent Woman, was critical of the song and dismissed it as a "chugging, faintly misty-eyed, middle of the road pop song".[\[37\]](#cite_note-independent.ie-37) Chris Richards of *[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")* panned the song as a "power ballad without much power".[\[38\]](#cite_note-38)

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Recognition and accolades")\]

Ernest Baker and Lauren Nostro of *[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_\(magazine\) "Complex (magazine)")* ranked "Diamonds" atop their list of The 10 Best Guilty Pleasure Songs of 2012 and wrote that, although the song is unlike Rihanna's louder, more anthemic songs, "apparently the world loves to see a softer side of her, too."[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) [Black Entertainment Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Entertainment_Television "Black Entertainment Television") placed the single at number 6 on their 50 Best Songs of 2012 list and called it one of Rihanna's most emotive performances.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40) UK [E! Online](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E!_Online "E! Online")'s reviewer named it the fifth best song of the year and said that Rihanna's vocal performance on the song validates the attention she had received since her breakthrough with "[Umbrella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umbrella_\(song\) "Umbrella (song)")".[\[41\]](#cite_note-41) *Irish Independent*'s Jim Hayes ranked it as the year's tenth-best song and described it as "a laid back slow burner that invades and refuses to leave".[\[42\]](#cite_note-II-42) A reviewer from *The Huffington Post* named "Diamonds" one of The 12 Best Songs by Women in 2012\.[\[43\]](#cite_note-43)

At the ASCAP Pop Music Awards, the [American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_of_Composers,_Authors_and_Publishers "American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers") (ASCAP) recognized it as one of the most performed songs of 2013[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) and 2014 respectively.[\[45\]](#cite_note-45) "Diamonds" received the *Billboard* accolade for Top R&B Song at the [2013 award ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Billboard_Music_Awards "2013 Billboard Music Awards") held at the [MGM Grand Garden Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MGM_Grand_Garden_Arena "MGM Grand Garden Arena") in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Valley "Las Vegas Valley").[\[46\]](#cite_note-46) At the [2013 BET Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BET_Awards_2013 "BET Awards 2013"), the song was nominated for the [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola") [Viewer's Choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BET_Award_for_Viewer's_Choice "BET Award for Viewer's Choice") accolade, however, it lost to "[Started from the Bottom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Started_from_the_Bottom "Started from the Bottom")" by [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(rapper\) "Drake (rapper)").[\[47\]](#cite_note-bet_2013-47) It also received nominations for Best International Song at the [NRJ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRJ_Music_Award "NRJ Music Award") of 2013 in France[\[48\]](#cite_note-48) and for Hit of the Year at the [2013 Echo Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Echo_Awards "2013 Echo Awards") in Germany.[\[49\]](#cite_note-49) "Diamonds" received a nomination for [Best Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Song "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Song") at the [2013 MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "2013 MTV Europe Music Awards").[\[50\]](#cite_note-50)

### North America

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: North America")\]

[![A blond woman wearing a jeweled black stage outfit plays a black guitar and sings into a microphone.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/MadonnaO2171023_%285_of_133%29_%2853270847219%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-MadonnaO2171023_%285_of_133%29_%2853270847219%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MadonnaO2171023_\(5_of_133\)_\(53270847219\)_\(cropped\).jpg)

"Diamonds" became Rihanna's twelfth number 1 on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), tying her with [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna "Madonna") (*pictured*) and [the Supremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Supremes "The Supremes") as the artists with the fifth-most number 1 singles in the chart's history.

In the US, "Diamonds" debuted at number 16 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and sold 133,000 copies in its first week.[\[51\]](#cite_note-51) In its fourth week, it climbed to number 8 on the chart and became Rihanna's twenty-third top-ten single.[\[52\]](#cite_note-TopTen-52) For the week ending December 1, 2012, the song became Rihanna's twelfth number 1 on the chart, which ended the nine-week reign of [Maroon 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maroon_5 "Maroon 5")'s "[One More Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_More_Night_\(Maroon_5_song\) "One More Night (Maroon 5 song)")".[\[53\]](#cite_note-us_sales-53) With the feat, Rihanna tied [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna "Madonna") and [the Supremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Supremes "The Supremes") as the [artists with the fifth-most number 1 singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_number-one_singles "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") in the chart's history. Rihanna also passed [Mariah Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey") as the female artist to mark twelve number 1 songs the fastest on the chart by achieving the feat in six years and seven months, which bested Carey's stretch of more than seven years.[\[54\]](#cite_note-number_1-54) "Diamonds" charted for three consecutive weeks atop the Hot 100, while her album *Unapologetic* topped the [*Billboard* 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"). As a result, Rihanna became only the second artist of 2012 to top both the *Billboard* singles and albums charts simultaneously; the first to do so was English singer [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele").[\[55\]](#cite_note-BillboardDouble-55)

On the [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart, "Diamonds" debuted at number 28\. In its fourth week, it climbed to number 10, becoming Rihanna's 19th top ten, breaking a tie with [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne") for the second-best sum in the list's 22-year history; only Mariah Carey (23) has more.[\[56\]](#cite_note-56) For the issue dated December 15, the song topped the chart, becoming Rihanna's tenth number 1 and placing second for female artists with the most chart toppers, only behind Mariah Carey (11).[\[57\]](#cite_note-Trust-57) On the [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40") chart, "Diamonds" debuted at number 29, extending Rihanna's lead as the artist with the most appearances on the chart.[\[58\]](#cite_note-PopDebut-58) On October 11, 2012, *Billboard* unveiled new methodology for the [Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") chart, newly factoring digital download sales and streaming data into the 50-position rankings, along with existing radio airplay data monitored by [Nielsen BDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_BDS "Nielsen BDS"). Due to this, "Diamonds" saw a huge leap from number 66 to number 1,[\[59\]](#cite_note-R&BNumberOne-59) marking Rihanna's second single as a lead artist to top the chart;[\[60\]](#cite_note-US_Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs-60) it topped the chart for fourteen consecutive weeks.[\[61\]](#cite_note-61) "Diamonds" topped the [Dance Club Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs") chart, becoming Rihanna's nineteenth number 1, tying her with [Janet Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Jackson "Janet Jackson") for the second-most number 1 songs in the chart's 36-year history. Only Madonna has more (49).[\[62\]](#cite_note-DanceNumberOne-62) "Diamonds" is, since 2024, [certified diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_certification "Music certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA).[\[63\]](#cite_note-RIAA-63)

In Canada, the song debuted at number 9 on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100") for the issue dated October 13, 2012\.[\[64\]](#cite_note-64) The song peaked at number 1 on the issue dated November 24, 2012, becoming Rihanna's sixth single to reach number 1 on the chart.[\[65\]](#cite_note-Canada-65) It remained atop of it for four consecutive weeks.[\[66\]](#cite_note-66) It was certified Gold by [Music Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Canada "Music Canada") denoting sales of over 40,000 copies.[\[67\]](#cite_note-Music_Canada-67)

## Music video

### Background and concept

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Background and concept")\]

> "With every song it's a different story, so the visuals are very specific to that story and that world. With 'Diamonds,' it was just a series of vignettes that we put together to help get the emotion across throughout the song 'cause the song changes and it builds, and there's no real way that you could do that."

— Rihanna explaining the concept for the music video.[\[90\]](#cite_note-MTVVena-90)

Rihanna began to film the [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "Diamonds" on October 21, 2012, at the [Mojave Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojave_Desert "Mojave Desert") in [Lancaster, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancaster,_California "Lancaster, California").[\[31\]](#cite_note-mtv1-31) It was directed by her regular collaborator [Anthony Mandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Mandler "Anthony Mandler"), who previously directed her videos for "[Russian Roulette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Roulette_\(Rihanna_song\) "Russian Roulette (Rihanna song)")" (2009) and "[Man Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_Down_\(song\) "Man Down (song)")" (2011).[\[31\]](#cite_note-mtv1-31) Photographs of the production leaked to the press the same day and showed Rihanna in a white and black dress in front of a fire. Ethan Sacks of the *New York Daily News* remarked that she "looked like a gem on the set of her video shoot."[\[91\]](#cite_note-91) Rihanna said that she wanted the video's abstract scenes to capture the appropriate emotion for the audience.[\[90\]](#cite_note-MTVVena-90) Mandler sought to create a "wider landscape" by suggesting and transfiguring ideas for viewers through the video: "\[T\]hey needed to feel like dream vignettes, like, when you wake up from a dream, you realize what you were dreaming about is not really what it was about, it was about something else."[\[92\]](#cite_note-Mandler-92) He also tried to relate the video's concept to Rihanna's personal life: "What's truth or fiction? You know 'Is she drowning, or is she in complete ecstasy? Are those hands coming apart, or are they finding each other?' ... we tried to bring up these deeper questions that relate to the song and her life and finding beauty in chaos and finding beauty in pain and finding pain in beauty."[\[92\]](#cite_note-Mandler-92) On November 7, a behind-the-scenes video was posted on [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")'s official website.[\[93\]](#cite_note-premiere-93) It featured Rihanna in a "leopard-print" robe as she emerged from a trailer and headed to the shooting set. The scenes were intercut with police officers who chase armed fighters. Rihanna stands in a deserted landscape in the video's other scenes.[\[93\]](#cite_note-premiere-93) The music video for "Diamonds" premiered November 8 on MTV. The video was also made available for [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") at Rihanna.MTV.com.[\[93\]](#cite_note-premiere-93) It was digitally released on November 14 via the [iTunes Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes_Store "ITunes Store").[\[94\]](#cite_note-94)

### Synopsis

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Diamonds_\(Rihanna_song\)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Synopsis")\]

[![A screenshot of two tattooed hands intertwining](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e1/Diamonds_video_shoot.png/330px-Diamonds_video_shoot.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Diamonds_video_shoot.png)

A screenshot from the music video showing Rihanna's hand intertwined with that of a heavily tattooed man. Some critics believed the arm of the man resembled that of [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown").[\[95\]](#cite_note-nbc_review-95)

The music video opens with a view of Rihanna lying in open waters, as other scenes of diamonds being rolled in a manner suggestive of making a joint are intercut – a scene reminiscent of the single's artwork. As the video progresses Rihanna is shown running on a highway. In a [black-and-white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black-and-white "Black-and-white") scene, Rihanna licks the joint and begins smoking it. The image fades to black as the song begins. Rihanna performs in the same black-and-white setting while in a black corset. Images of Rihanna on a bed in a room while singing are shown, with objects breaking, curtains falling and roses burning in [reverse effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backwards_masking "Backwards masking"). Rihanna is shown again on the highway, running away from what appears to be the headlights of a chasing car. She then stops as she looks up to the night sky at an [aurora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_\(astronomy\) "Aurora (astronomy)") view. Throughout the video, Rihanna's hand is shown intertwined with that of a heavily tattooed man, whose face is not shown in the video. As the second verse starts, Rihanna is shown in a desert where horses run freely. Scenes of a street battle are later shown, depicting burning cars and broken glass around the environment. As the video continues, the singer and her lover's hands are shown slowly slipping apart, with only their fingertips touching towards the conclusion of the video. The video ends with Rihanna once again floating alone in the open waters.

Wikipedia confirms the key details of Rihanna's "Diamonds" video (dir. Anthony Mandler, 2012): it opens with Rihanna floating in dark open waters, features explicitly **black-and-white scenes**, dark bedroom scenes with burning roses and falling curtains, pale desert scenes (horses, street battle), bright highway headlight scenes — and it **ends by returning to the dark open waters**.

Now comparing the measured barcode profile against that:

| Barcode feature | Diamonds match |
|---|---|
| Max chroma spread only 25/255 — essentially monochrome | Famous sepia/warm B&W grading of the video |
| Hue ~50–58° at low saturation (warm yellow-olive), near-neutral highlights | Textbook sepia: warm-tinted shadows, neutral whites |
| Dark warm first stripe (rgb 55,53,40) | Opens on dark open water |
| Bright neutral-white cluster at 74–95% (lum jumps to ~115) | Bright pale desert daylight / washed-out sky scenes late in the video |
| Very dark final stripe (rgb 37,35,27) | Ends with Rihanna floating alone in dark water again |

The other muted candidates don't fit: *Rolling in the Deep* is amber/tungsten-lit color (channel spread well above 40, hue ~35°), and *Let Her Go* has warm colored stage lighting; the rest (Baby, Bad Romance, Blank Space, Shape of You, Girls Like You, Thinking Out Loud, Treat You Better) are far too colorful to ever produce a barcode whose most saturated pixel is only ~10% saturated.

**Answer: J**
